rounds.text: Alfred Herbert (India) Ltd presents a compelling case for being severely under-appreciated, trading at a remarkably low P/E ratio of 5.91x alongside a price-to-book ratio of just 0.37x against a book value of ₹ 7,253 [E1, E2]. This valuation sits at a stark discount compared to sector benchmarks, where the stock's P/E of 0.45x and EV/EBITDA of 0.3x lag far behind sector medians of 25.26x and 21.55x respectively [E6, E11]. Underlying fundamentals display explosive momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 336% and profit growth of 467%, dramatically outpacing long-term trends [E17, E21]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free, boasts a massive free cash flow of ₹ 444 Cr, and benefits from a supportive financial services sector tailwind with a score of +0.83 [E32, E52, E66]. Results are rapidly improving with a net profit surge of 30800% year-over-year while the price remains depressed below its moving averages, showcasing a classic disconnect between accelerating fundamentals and stale sentiment [E43, E59, E65]. Conceded: [E30] operating cash flow is negative at ₹ -64 Cr in Mar 2026, [E43] the price trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and [E57] earnings include other income of ₹ 481 Cr.
